title: Instrumentation QuickKit: Low-Latency Inference Observability
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, actionable playkit for instrumenting low-latency token-serving pipelines. Focus is on small, high-signal metrics and minimal-trace overhead that help engineers diagnose tail-latency, batching anomalies, and cache regressions quickly. Draft notes / checklist for implementation and dashboard layout.

Quick wins (30–90m):
- Add token_emit_rate and inflight_batch_size_p95 to the existing metrics emitter. Low cost, immediate insight into batching behavior.
- Expose kv_cache_hit_ratio_v2 (per-model, per-route) from the cache layer with tags: model, route, region.
- Create a short dashboard panel: heatmap(batch_size vs p99 latency) for the last 6 hours.

Metric definitions (canonical names + intent):
- token_emit_rate: gauge, tokens/sec emitted by the runtime per route. Intent: detect throughput collapse and backpressure.
- inflight_batch_size_{p50,p95,p99}: histogram summaries of batches actually dispatched to the accelerator. Intent: correlate batch size to latency.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio_v2: ratio (hits / requests) for KV/prefix caching; include tag cached_prefix_len. Intent: detect cache churn or ineffective prefixes.
- route_fallback_rate: count / minute of requests hitting a fallback model or region. Intent: surface degraded routing.
- async_response_backpressure_count: counter for requests queued due to executor backpressure. Intent: shows when request queueing is in play (correlate with cpu/gpu util).
- per_token_cost_estimate_usd: derived metric (tokens * model_unit_cost); for dashboards to tie performance to spend.

Tracing guidance (span design, attributes, sampling):
- Top-level span: request_lifecycle. Child spans: routing_decision, prefix_lookup, batch_assemble, kernel_dispatch, kv_store_op, streaming_writer. Keep span durations short (avoid adding sleeps in spans).
- Important attributes on request_lifecycle: request_id, customer_id (hashed), route, model_name, sequence_length, trace_mode (sync|streaming).
- kernel_dispatch span should carry: batch_id, batch_size, gpu_id, quantization_profile. That ties OS/scheduler events to latency.
- Sampling: default head-sampling 1% for production, dynamic increase to 20% for error_rate>0.5% or when route_fallback_rate spikes. Also support on-demand trace capture by passing header X-Trace-Force (dev only).
- Span truncation policy: drop stack frames >50ms to keep traces small. For long-running streaming sessions, emit a short heartbeat span every 5s instead of capturing all micro-spans.

Dashboard layout notes (single-page, top-to-bottom):
1) Health row: global error_rate, route_fallback_rate, async_response_backpressure_count, per_token_cost_estimate_usd (last 1h).
2) Latency row: p50/p95/p99 latency by route & model, heatmap(batch_size vs p99 latency).
3) Throughput row: token_emit_rate, requests/sec, inflight_batch_size distribution, GPU-scheduler-wait_ms (if available).
4) Cache row: kv_cache_hit_ratio_v2 (by prefix_len), cache_eviction_rate, cache_fill_latency_ms.
5) Traces & Alerts row: trace-sample-rate, recent traces list (linked), alerts firing.

Widget tips and pruning guidance:
- Prefer percentiles over averages for latency widgets. Keep p95/p99 for daily ops, p50 for quick sanity checks.
- Use heatmaps for batch size analysis. Keep resolution coarse (8 bins) to reduce cardinality.
- Aggregate per-route widgets by tier (hosted/dedicated/private) to avoid exploded series counts.
- Retention: detailed histogram buckets for 48h, rolled-up summaries (p50/p95/p99) for 30d.

Alerting suggestions (initial thresholds):
- p99 latency increase > 2x vs 1h baseline for a route -> warn.
- route_fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m -> page (indicates upstream capacity or model load problem).
- kv_cache_hit_ratio_v2 drops >20% vs 1h baseline -> warn.
- async_response_backpressure_count > 50 concurrently -> page.

Operational play examples:
- Investigating tail latency: check heatmap -> if batch_size skewed to 1 and p99 high, check scheduler preemption and prefix_lookup latency.
- If token_emit_rate drops and cpu/gpu util low -> inspect routing_decision spans for misrouted traffic (route_tag mismatch).
- Cache regressions: follow cache_fill_latency_ms + kv_cache_hit_ratio_v2; correlate with recent model rollouts (linked to release tags).

Implementation checklist (owners / short tasks):
- [ ] runtime: implement token_emit_rate (Diego) -> PR created: github.com/.../678 (reference).
- [ ] cache layer: kv_cache_hit_ratio_v2 + cached_prefix_len tag (Priya).
- [ ] tracing: add kernel_dispatch attributes and sampling knobs (Lena).
- [ ] dashboards: create single-page low-latency view and add to shared dashboards (Ava).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Sampling overhead vs signal: is 1% base enough for multi-tenant hosted traffic? Suggest trial with 2% for 2 weeks and evaluate sample-quality.
- Privacy: customer_id must be hashed and reversible only via support SRE escrow. Confirm with security.
- Cardinality: how many route/model tag combos will we have? Consider a route-tag quota and aggregated rollups for low-volume routes.

Next steps and quick experiments:
- Run 48h experiment with: base sampling 2%, full tracing for one canary route for 24h, and kv_cache_hit_ratio_v2 metrics enabled cluster-wide. Measure sampling cost and trace size. (JIRA: JIRA-INF-2045)
- Ship token_emit_rate and small dashboard; evaluate if ops pages detect more regressions during weekly load tests.

Notes to self: keep this doc small and iterate. If the quick-kit works, convert parts to the longer observability handbook and standard metric contracts.

References (internal):
- Canaries: CONFLUENCE-9123 (canary rollout patterns)
- Tracing design notes: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/design-tracing.md
